what_happened: The job changed the queue drain so that re-reads of "needs-accepting" items no longer count toward the drain job limit. The verifier rejected it at the final verdict. One of 6 acceptance criteria was unmet. That criterion says that with the `st.started` decrement removed from the needs-accepting arm of `run_job`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` fails on the new test (b not run, Stop::JobLimit), and that the recorded check output shows both that failing run and the passing run with the fix. There was one major finding: the failing run without the fix appears in nothing the verifier received. No failed checks are listed. The fix itself is not reported as wrong. This is the same gap that rejected the earlier attempt at this work (job 20261103-193428-df2m).
cause: The criterion asks for proof that exists only if someone runs the tests against a tree with the fix removed. Athena's checks run once, on the final tree, and the verifier sees only those results, the diff and the criteria. The only place the without-fix run could be recorded is the producer's own report, which the verifier does not receive. So a correct producer cannot satisfy the criterion through any channel the verifier reads. The reading keeps writing "fails without the fix" criteria with no mechanism that produces that evidence. The previous attempt was rejected on the same criterion, and the re-ask repeated the criterion unchanged instead of providing an evidence path. This is an inference, since the producer's report is not in the stored fields.
prevention: Make "fails without the fix" a check that Athena runs itself. For a bug-fix job, Athena would run the new or changed tests against the base tree's production code, with the job's test files overlaid, and record the failing output as a named check. It would then run them on the final tree. The verifier would receive both results as recorded check output. The reading would then be required to phrase such criteria in terms of that check, and not as producer-reported evidence. As a stopgap, the reading step should refuse any criterion whose evidence only the producer can supply.
proposed_request: Add an automatic "fails without the fix" check to Athena's verification, so that bug-fix jobs can be judged on it. Outcome: when a job's acceptance criteria say its new or changed tests must fail without the fix, Athena itself runs those tests against the base commit's production code with the job's test files overlaid, records the failing output as a named check in the job's check records, and the verifier receives that record next to the normal passing run on the final tree. The producer must not be required to supply this evidence. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fixture job whose test fails on the base code and passes on the final tree shows both runs in the recorded checks; (2) a fixture where the test passes on the base code too shows the check recorded as failed, with the reason; (3) the verifier brief tells the verifier to read this check for such criteria; (4) a job with no such criterion runs no extra check; (5) cargo fmt --check, clippy and cargo test --workspace pass; (6) CHANGELOG has an entry. After it lands, re-ask job 20261103-222737-zzsr: don't count needs-accepting re-reads toward the drain job limit, with a test that fails on the old `run_job` counter (b not run, Stop::JobLimit).
